messages.subject: queue with group delay
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I am doing a simulation of the patient-path to an outpatient clinic:

Whenever a patient requests to be submitted to the clinic, a letter from a physician with this request will be sent to the clinic. Administrative staff will print out this letter and put it in a certain mailbox. This mailbox is emptied by a doctor in order to perform triage (i.e. determining the priority of patients' treatments based on the severity of their condition). This usually happens once every 1 to 3 days, and takes no more than a couple of hours. After this, the patient is called by the administrative staff and is scheduled for an appointment.

I am pretty new to this package and my problem is the following:

How can I make sure the mailbox is emptied with a timeout=(function() rgamma(1, shape = 2, rate = 0.1)), which should vary every time?
I feel as if I should use batch() as I've done below, but it obviously doesn't work since batch() only accepts a numeric (10000 could be any number that is big enough to ensure it is only emptied when the doctor arrives).

triage <- trajectory("Patient's path") %>%
  log_("arrive at queue") %>%
  batch(10000, timeout=(function() rgamma(1, shape = 2, rate = 0.1))) %>%
  log_("triage") %>%
  seize("triage_doctor", 1) %>%
  timeout(function() rgamma(1, shape = 2, rate = 0.8)) %>%
  release("triage_doctor", 1) %>%
  separate() %>%
  seize("administrative_empl",1) %>%
  log_("patient is being called") %>%
  timeout(0.1) %>%
  log_("Appointment is made") %>%
  release("administrative_empl", 1)

env <- simmer()  %>%
  add_resource("triage_doctor", capacity = 1) %>%
  add_resource("administrative_empl", capacity = 1) %>%
  add_generator("person", triage, function() rpois(1, 2)) %>%
  run(800)

I've also tried the following things:
- Taking the function out of batch(): but that either results in a constant timeout for every batch, or in a constant delay for every patient.
- Using synchronize(): I don't even know what I was thinking while using this.
- Doint something with send(), trap() and wait(): got no clue how though.

Does anyone have an idea how to solve this?

Thanks in advance,

Kind regards,

Dominique

messages.body_plain:
Hi Dominique,

You have a couple of options. Both of them involve the definition of a secondary trajectory for managing the mailbox. Given your description, and assuming that, whenever it is checked, the mailbox is emptied completely, I would use trap-wait-send as follows:

triage <- trajectory("Patient's path") %>%
  log_("arrive at queue"

) %>%
  trap("check mailbox") %>%
  wait() %>%
  log_("triage")
  # etc.

mailbox <- trajectory() %>%
  timeout(function() rgamma(1, shape = 2, rate = 0.1)) %>%
  send("check mailbox") %>%
  rollback(2, Inf)

env <- simmer()  %>%
  add_resource("triage_doctor", capacity = 1) %>%
  add_resource("administrative_empl", capacity = 1) %>%
  add_generator("person", triage, function() rpois(1, 2)) %>%
  add_generator("mailbox", mailbox, at(0)) %>%
  run(800)

If at some point you need a finer-grained control of the number of letters read at a time, then I would define a new resource for the mailbox with capacity=0. Then, the trap-wait would be replaced by a seize-set_capacity(0) of that resource, and the send activity, by a set_capacity(n), where n is the required number of letters.

Regards,
Iñaki
​

Just another point to note in your solution design (which happens to be a problem I'm running into).

Since Markovian arrival distributions have additive means, it is MUCH simpler to NOT create different arrival generators for the same phenomena. For example, the arrival rate of emergency room patients = the weighted average of the arrival rates for gun shot wounds vs all non-gun shot wounds. This could be modeled in 2 ways:
1) Create two trajectories.
2) Create a single arrivel trajectory, and assign an attribute 'Gun Shot Wound' based on the historical proportion that gun shot wounds comprise of total emergency room patients.

While option 1 is intuitive, it doesn't scale to multiple attributes. For example, if I had 10 'reasons' to visit the emergency room (attribute 1), and I wanted to model 10 phases of the moon (attribute 2), I would need to create 100 generators. (Not tenable)

So it would be GREAT if we can reference the attribute for 'this' trajectory and use it as an input to functions.

messages.subject: Avoiding memory/reference leaks inside function (?)
messages.body_plain:
Good afternoon,

I am attempting to wrap a simmer DES (in this case, a psychiatric hospital with a waiting list) inside a function which would pass various parameters (in this case, total number of incoming admissions, number of beds, average length of stay, and replications) to the simulation for modeling, and return the 5th, 50th and 95th percentile for results of interest.

The simulation runs for 5 "years", but I truncate the last year of data, bind the list of simulation results together, and process the results in the function itself, so the actual result of the function is only a small data table.

The end goal is to use mapply to start with a data table of these starting parameters, and build a data table of results from those parameters automatically.

Everything seems to work fine, but I've noticed that RAM consistently creeps upward  -- to the point where, if I have enough parameters and replications, my 32 GB machine is completely consumed and the simulation aborts due to lack of memory.

I'm suspecting that there is some kind of reference leak in the simulation environment. Definitely not an R expert, so I'm struggling to figure out how to clean these up -- i.e., presumably deleting the simulation results in the environment they are accumulating.

For simplicity, I am not using lapply or mclapply in the function itself -- just a for loop. Simplified code is attached to demonstrate the issue.

Thanks for your time and consideration.

Very respectfully,
Franz Fuchs
franz...@wyo.gov

Hi, this issue has been solved on GitHub. As I said in my last mail, I found another problem which prevents the object's destructor from being called in some circumstances. Unfortunately, there is nothing we can do about it right now, because the bug is in magrittr or Rcpp, not in simmer (see the report <https://github.com/tidyverse/magrittr/issues/146>).

Now, what can you do to prevent your machine from running out of memory?
Use the current master branch on GitHub (you can install it with devtools::install_github) until we roll out a new release (at the end of the month, probably).
I recommend you to reset your environment once you've extracted the information needed inside your loop, that is: create the env, run it, call get_mon_whatever, and then call reset(env).
Regards,
Iñaki

messages.subject: Variable number of ongoing tasks
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have a problem where the number of transactions changes and I cannot figure out how best to implement it in simmer.

Let's say there are a lot of tasks waiting to be implemented, each taking an integer number of days (with a Poisson distribution).

There are, say, 10 people available.

A task may require more than one person (most require a single person).

I want to keep all people busy every day.  The number of tasks on any given day is likely to vary.

An example case: on a given day there may be 6 people already committed to tasks.  The remaining 4 people may start between 1 task (requiring 4 people), 4 tasks (each requiring one person) or some combination.

The task duration and number of people required are chosen at random (this is not true in reality, but I am trying to keep things simple).

I have created scripts with:

add_resource("person", capacity=10)

and with

add_resource("person_1", capacity=1)
add_resource("person_2", capacity=1)
etc

and a queue for cases where insufficient people are available for the task

But I can never keep everybody occupied.

I am trying to keep user written functions to a minimum, i.e., rely on simmer functions and options.  But this approach does not appear possible.

Suggestions welcome.

Iñaki,

Thanks for the prompt reply.

There was a bug in my code caused by a misunderstanding on my part.  I thought the trajectory name was more of a comment.  In the Introduction to simmer Vignette, the code:

patient <- trajectory("patients' path") %>%

has patient with and without an s, but always uses it without an s

add_generator("patient", patient, function() rnorm(1, 10, 2))

Changing the code below to use add_generator("feature", feature, at(rep(0, 1e2))) produces very different behavior.

Anyway major problem solved :-)
It takes a couple of time steps for the queue to fill, but this is not a problem.

Is there a way to create an infinite queue of pending tasks without flooding the pipeline at the start?

library(gamlss.tr <http://gamlss.tr>)
library("simmer")

# Create a zero truncated Poisson distribution
gen.trun(family=PO)

env=simmer("impl_env")

feature=trajectory("feature imp") %>%
    set_attribute("num_dev", function() rPOtr(1, 2)) %>%
    seize("developer", function(attrs) attrs[["num_dev"]]) %>%
    timeout(function() rPOtr(1, 2)) %>%
    release("developer", function(attrs) attrs[["num_dev"]])

env %>%
    add_resource("developer", 10) %>%
    add_generator("feature imp", feature, at(rep(0, 1e2)))

env %>%
    run(until=20)

env %>%
    get_mon_arrivals

env %>%
    get_mon_resources

messages.subject: problems with select()
messages.body_plain:
I was going over http://r-simmer.org/articles/C-trajectories.html  Advanced Trajectory Usage
and the code below, which is from section select()

==================================================================
library(simmer)
patient_traj <- trajectory <http://r-simmer.org/reference/trajectory.html>(name = "patient_trajectory") %>%
  set_attribute <http://r-simmer.org/reference/set_attribute.html>("resource", function() sample(1:3, 1)) %>%
  select <http://r-simmer.org/reference/select.html>(resources = function(attrs) paste0("doctor", attrs["resource"])) %>%
  seize_selected <http://r-simmer.org/reference/seize.html>(amount = 1) %>%
  timeout <http://r-simmer.org/reference/timeout.html>(5) %>%
  release_selected <http://r-simmer.org/reference/seize.html>(amount = 1)

env <- simmer <http://r-simmer.org/reference/simmer.html>() %>%
  add_resource <http://r-simmer.org/reference/add_resource.html>("doctor1", capacity = 1) %>%
  add_resource <http://r-simmer.org/reference/add_resource.html>("doctor2", capacity = 1) %>%
  add_resource <http://r-simmer.org/reference/add_resource.html>("doctor3", capacity = 1) %>%
  add_generator <http://r-simmer.org/reference/add_generator.html>("patient", patient_traj, at <http://r-simmer.org/reference/at.html>(0, 1, 2), mon = 2) %>%
  run <http://r-simmer.org/reference/run.html>()

get_mon_attributes <http://r-simmer.org/reference/get_mon.html>(env)
============================================================
produces the following error:
Error in UseMethod("select_") :
  no applicable method for 'select_' applied to an object of class "c('trajectory', 'R6')"
Why is that? How does simmer know that this is not select() from package dplyr?

Hi Shawn,

I'm quite impressed, that's a great work! About the runtime, some kind of progress report is a feature that I think it's very interesting for long runs and easy to implement in simmer as an option. I'll definitely take a look at this. In the meantime, Mark's suggestions are to be considered.

Another simpler approach that comes to my mind, a more... heuristic approach, would be to run the model in steps. For instance, let's say that the selected simulation time is 5000. You can run(until=1000), report back to the user, run(until=2000), report back... and finally run(until=5000). Because if you increase the time, the simulation just continues from the last step. So the web interface would show: 0%, 20%, 40%... The penalty in terms of total execution time should be very small.
